packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-07 - unverified image reading (blind first reader)

Exposure statement: no proposed identification of the work or author was in my context. I did nothing beyond the stated rules (I listed the packet directory only to get image filenames and compared PROMPT.md files across packets).

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Two narrow vertical parchment strips, labelled "A" and "B" by the photographer, photographed on both sides with a 17 cm ruler. Overview image-001 = face 1 (A left, B right); overview image-004 = face 2 (B left, A right). Tiles: image-002/003 (face 1, top/bottom), image-005/006 (face 2, top/bottom).
- The two strips are adjacent pieces of the same leaf cut vertically (binding strips): the text runs across the cut. On face 1, A carries line beginnings (with left margin and ruling pricks) and B the continuation (e.g. A "lo-sopho" + B "rum"). On face 2, B carries most of the line and A the line ends plus right margin. The right side of the line (face 1) / left side (face 2) is lost beyond the strips.
- Single column visible (a column of perhaps 6-7 cm width; full width not preserved). About 16-17 lines survive per face. Protogothic / early Gothic book hand, brown ink. Ruled in drypoint/plummet.
- Enlarged plain ink capitals (not red as far as visible) at sentence starts: "Hec", "Hic", "Quia" on face 1; "Igitur", "Sub", "Hec", and a marginal capital at the start of the last line of face 2. No rubrics, no running titles, no glosses seen.
- Pencil numbers on face 2: "4967" (strip B, lower) and "496[?]" (strip A, right margin) - modern.
- Content (interpretation): continuous prose, with scripture-like phrases woven in; it appears to be expository/homiletic prose. Not identified.

SPANS SELECTED: all surviving lines on both faces, reading A+B together as one line where the text visibly joins. Line numbers are counted from the top of each tile; the joined line is given as A-part | B-part (face 1) or B-part | A-part (face 2). Overlaps: image-003 lines 1-4 = image-002 lines 13-16; image-006 lines 1-4 = image-005 lines 15-18.

LIMITATIONS
- Only a vertical slice of the column survives; every line is truncated on one side (face 1 right; face 2 left). The join between A and B is a knife cut, and one or two letters at the cut are often lost or uncertain.
- My joining of A and B parts into single lines assumes the strips are aligned as photographed; in the photos they are slightly offset vertically, so A/B line pairing could be off by one line in places (the "lo-sopho|rum" and "p(ro)tecti|one" joins support the alignment used on face 1; face 2 alignment is less certain).
- Readings with (?) are uncertain; expansions in parentheses are mine. Scripture-like phrases are transcribed only as far as letters are visible.
- A wider view of any neighbouring strips from the same leaf would restore the missing part of the lines.
